references.text: God's answer to Moses' prayer to see His glory, where God explains that no one can see His face and live.
The fulfillment of Moses' prayer, where the Lord comes down in the cloud and proclaims His name and His glory.
A previous revelation of God's glory (כָּבוֹד) on Mount Sinai, which Moses experienced.
God's glory fills the temple, a visible manifestation of the same glory Moses asked to see.
Isaiah's vision of the Lord's glory in the temple, where the seraphim cry out about His holiness.
Ezekiel's vision of the appearance of the Lord's glory, a revelation of the divine glory.
The Word became flesh and we saw His glory (δόξαν) – God's glory revealed in Christ.
No one has ever seen God, but the Son has made Him known – an answer to what Moses sought.
Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father, and Jesus answers that whoever has seen Him has seen the Father.
We behold the Lord's glory with unveiled face and are transformed – a parallel to Moses' experience.
The knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ – the fulfillment of the revelation Moses sought.
The Son is the radiance of God's glory – the ultimate revelation of what Moses asked to see.
Connects Moses' prayer to see God's glory with the liturgical order that makes God's glory visible to the people.
